en: So in order to make sure that when we delete
an item, we also update the available places
list and we re-add the deleted item to that
list,
we have to tweak the response we send back
in that delete request handler.
Because whilst an empty response is great to
delete the item or some item that was
responsible for sending the delete request,
it's not enough if we also wanna perform
such an out-of-band swap.
And that is indeed what I wanna do here.
I wanna do both. I wanna send back an empty
response body essentially for this
element here that sent the DELETE request.
But at the same time, I wanna attach some
other content that should be used for an
out-of-band swap.
And that is something you can do.
Here I can simply
repeat the code from my POST route handler
and derive the available locations as a
first step
like this by copying this constant.
And then I'll return this unordered list
with the available locations just as I did
it before
with that
out-of-band swap attribute added to it.
Now you might say, okay, great, but now it's
not an empty response anymore, but you would
be wrong.
This part of the response body
is meant to be used in an out-of-band swap.
And the remaining part of the response body
is then essentially nothing.
So the element that sent the DELETE request
in the end still gets back an empty
response. Because the non-empty part is used
for this out-of-band swap.
And therefore, by making this simple
adjustment, we can again save everything,
but we'll now be able to switch these items
between these 2 lists.
And as I remove an item from the top list,
it's re-added to the bottom list and vice
versa.
And that's therefore now working the way it
should work here.
